lines.text: A square, a circle, a smaller square, a smaller circle. Like nesting dolls!
lines.caption: A square, a circle, a smaller square, a smaller circle. Like nesting dolls!

lines.text: The shaded ring looks tricky. <short pause> But there's a neat surprise hiding inside.
lines.caption: The shaded ring looks tricky. But there's a neat surprise hiding inside.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the ring's area together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the ring's area together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A circle fits inside a square with side length eight.
lines.caption: A circle fits inside a square with side length eight.

lines.text: A smaller square has its corners on that circle. A smaller circle fits inside that square.
lines.caption: A smaller square has its corners on that circle. A smaller circle fits inside that square.

lines.text: What is the area of the shaded ring between the two circles?
lines.caption: What is the area of the shaded ring between the two circles?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what are we really looking for?
lines.caption: So what are we really looking for?

lines.text: The ring is the big circle, take away the small circle.
lines.caption: The ring is the big circle, take away the small circle.

lines.text: So we need the area of each circle. And for that, we need each radius.
lines.caption: So we need the area of each circle. And for that, we need each radius.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's start with the big circle.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's start with the big circle.

lines.text: It fits snugly in the square, so its diameter equals the side. That's eight.
lines.caption: It fits snugly in the square, so its diameter equals the side. That's eight.

lines.text: So its radius is four. Pi times four squared is sixteen pi.
lines.caption: So its radius is four. Pi times four squared is sixteen pi.

lines.text: Now the small square. Its corners touch the big circle.
lines.caption: Now the small square. Its corners touch the big circle.

lines.text: So its diagonal goes right across the circle. The diagonal is a diameter, eight!
lines.caption: So its diagonal goes right across the circle. The diagonal is a diameter, eight!

lines.text: The diagonal and two sides of the small square make a right triangle.
lines.caption: The diagonal and two sides of the small square make a right triangle.

lines.text: Pythagoras says side squared plus side squared equals eight squared, which is sixty-four.
lines.caption: Pythagoras says side squared plus side squared equals eight squared, which is sixty-four.

lines.text: So side squared is thirty-two. The side is root thirty-two.
lines.caption: So side squared is thirty-two. The side is root thirty-two.

lines.text: Thirty-two is sixteen times two, so that's four root two.
lines.caption: Thirty-two is sixteen times two, so that's four root two.

lines.text: The small circle fits snugly in the small square. So its diameter is four root two.
lines.caption: The small circle fits snugly in the small square. So its diameter is four root two.

lines.text: Its radius is half of that, two root two.
lines.caption: Its radius is half of that, two root two.

lines.text: Two root two, squared, is four times two. That's eight. So the small circle is eight pi.
lines.caption: Two root two, squared, is four times two. That's eight. So the small circle is eight pi.

lines.text: The ring is sixteen pi minus eight pi.
lines.caption: The ring is sixteen pi minus eight pi.

lines.text: That's eight pi! The answer is B.
lines.caption: That's eight pi! The answer is B.

lines.text: Here's a clever way, with no root two at all.
lines.caption: Here's a clever way, with no root two at all.

lines.text: In the picture, the small square's corners sit at the middle of each side of the big square.
lines.caption: In the picture, the small square's corners sit at the middle of each side of the big square.

lines.text: Now fold the four corner triangles inward. They cover the small square exactly!
lines.caption: Now fold the four corner triangles inward. They cover the small square exactly!

lines.text: Each corner triangle is half of four times four. That's eight. Four of them make thirty-two.
lines.caption: Each corner triangle is half of four times four. That's eight. Four of them make thirty-two.

lines.text: So the small square is half of the big square. Thirty-two out of sixty-four.
lines.caption: So the small square is half of the big square. Thirty-two out of sixty-four.

lines.text: Now turn the small square forty-five degrees. It's a shrunk copy of the big picture!
lines.caption: Now turn the small square forty-five degrees. It's a shrunk copy of the big picture!

lines.text: Same shape, so every area shrinks the same way. The square's area halved, so the circle's does too.
lines.caption: Same shape, so every area shrinks the same way. The square's area halved, so the circle's does too.

lines.text: Half of sixteen pi is eight pi. That's the small circle.
lines.caption: Half of sixteen pi is eight pi. That's the small circle.

lines.text: So the ring is the other half. Eight pi again! The ring and the small circle are equal.
lines.caption: So the ring is the other half. Eight pi again! The ring and the small circle are equal.

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When shapes nest inside each other, look for a shrunk copy.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When shapes nest inside each other, look for a shrunk copy.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice C, twelve pi, is what you'd get with a small radius of two. Sixteen pi minus four pi.
lines.caption: Choice C, twelve pi, is what you'd get with a small radius of two. Sixteen pi minus four pi.

lines.text: But the small square's side isn't four, it's four root two. The AREA halves, not the radius.
lines.caption: But the small square's side isn't four, it's four root two. The AREA halves, not the radius.

lines.text: Choice D, sixteen pi, is just the big circle. It forgets to take away the small one.
lines.caption: Choice D, sixteen pi, is just the big circle. It forgets to take away the small one.

lines.text: Choice E, twenty-four pi, adds the two circles instead of subtracting.
lines.caption: Choice E, twenty-four pi, adds the two circles instead of subtracting.

lines.text: Choice A, four pi, halves one time too many. That's the area of the NEXT circle in, not our ring.
lines.caption: Choice A, four pi, halves one time too many. That's the area of the NEXT circle in, not our ring.

lines.text: So here's a habit: the ring is the big circle MINUS the small circle.
lines.caption: So here's a habit: the ring is the big circle MINUS the small circle.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Let's go one level deeper.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Let's go one level deeper.

lines.text: The big square now has a side of twelve. Inside it sit a circle, a square, a circle, a square, and a circle.
lines.caption: The big square now has a side of twelve. Inside it sit a circle, a square, a circle, a square, and a circle.

lines.text: Each circle fits snugly in its square. Each square has its corners on the circle around it.
lines.caption: Each circle fits snugly in its square. Each square has its corners on the circle around it.

lines.text: Shade everything between the biggest circle and the smallest circle. What is its area?
lines.caption: Shade everything between the biggest circle and the smallest circle. What is its area?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The big circle has radius six. Pi times six squared is thirty-six pi.
lines.caption: Let's check. The big circle has radius six. Pi times six squared is thirty-six pi.

lines.text: Circle, square, circle: each time, the circle's area halves. So the middle circle is eighteen pi.
lines.caption: Circle, square, circle: each time, the circle's area halves. So the middle circle is eighteen pi.

lines.text: One more level in, and the smallest circle is nine pi.
lines.caption: One more level in, and the smallest circle is nine pi.

lines.text: Thirty-six pi minus nine pi is twenty-seven pi!
lines.caption: Thirty-six pi minus nine pi is twenty-seven pi!

lines.text: Double-check: the area went down to one fourth, so the radius is half of six. That's three.
lines.caption: Double-check: the area went down to one fourth, so the radius is half of six. That's three.

lines.text: Pi times three squared is nine pi. It matches!
lines.caption: Pi times three squared is nine pi. It matches!

lines.text: If you found twenty-seven pi, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found twenty-seven pi, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Square in a circle: its diagonal is the diameter. Circle in a square: its diameter is the side.
lines.caption: Square in a circle: its diagonal is the diameter. Circle in a square: its diameter is the side.

lines.text: And circle, square, circle: the inner circle has exactly half the AREA of the outer one.
lines.caption: And circle, square, circle: the inner circle has exactly half the AREA of the outer one.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
